item.title: Flights disrupted at NYC-area airports due to equipment outage, FAA says
item.description: Flights at Newark Liberty International, John F. Kennedy International and LaGuardia airports are delayed due to an equipment outage, the FAA says.

item.title: Paramount Skydance reaches antitrust deal with states over Warner Bros. Discovery purchase
item.description: Paramount's agreement with 12 state attorneys general paves the way for the company to complete its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

item.title: Family tied to suspected Chinese spy gave $4.4M to Newsom, Calif. politicians
item.description: C.C. Yin's family has donated nearly $3 million to state-level California political causes and an additional $1,455,027 to federal campaigns.

item.title: Trump announces "AI Force" and plans to unveil "AI Czar"; Nvidia CEO dismisses AI concerns
item.description: President Trump on Saturday announced he is forming an "AI Force" and vowed not to allow a slowdown of AI development despite several recent warnings from industry insiders about the technology's rapid growth. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is brushing off apocalyptic concerns about AI. Andrew Pantazi, associate editor of breaking news for Axios, joins CBS News to discuss Trump's plans, then CBS News' Jo Ling Kent and Anthony Salvanto unpack Huang's comments and Americans' feelings on AI.

item.title: Paramount Skydance settles with 12 states over acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday announced details of a settlement reached between Paramount Skydance and 12 states over the company's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Paramount Skydance is the parent company of CBS News.

item.title: "Pictures to hurt you": A war photographer's final testament to Vietnam
item.description: "I want my pictures to hurt," British war photographer Sir Don McCullin told CBS News ahead of the publication of his final book: "Vietnam."

item.title: Iran warns new U.S. assault would see it expand "geography of the war"
item.description: As President Trump touts a looming decision on his next move in the war, Tehran says any "new aggression" would be met with different weapons in new places.

item.title: War photographer Don McCullin revisits harrowing assignment: "I want my pictures to hurt you"
item.description: For more than 50 years, legendary war photographer Don McCullin has documented conflict on battlefields across the globe. Now, at 90, he revisits the assignment that shaped him as a reporter — and scarred him as a man. All images in the feature are (c) Don McCullin and featured in the book Vietnam published by GOST Books.

item.title: How data centers and immigration policy are impacting voters ahead of the 2026 midterms
item.description: A Texas rancher who voted for President Trump in 2024 told CBS News' Norah O'Donnell that the rapid development of AI data centers could impact how he votes in the midterms. Meanwhile, Florida Rep. María Elvira Salazar, a Republican, warned about Hispanic voters' take on President Trump's immigration policies. CBS News' Fin Gomez has more.

item.title: Police officer wounded in shooting near synagogue on Yom Kippur
item.description: Police have not said what led to the shooting or whether the synagogue or Jewish community was targeted.

item.title: Presidential TV pool suspended after Trump bans CNN
item.description: CNN was set to provide pool coverage on Monday and accompany President Trump on a trip to New York City, but there will not be a network TV pool team traveling with him.

item.title: Betting apps face allegations of fueling addictive behavior, putting gambling addicts at higher risk
item.description: Betting apps are being accused of fueling addictive behavior, especially for vulnerable gamblers. Alex Klavens, a data journalist for The New York Times, interviewed former DraftKings employees who claim the platform may have been targeting addicts. He joins CBS News 24/7 to discuss his findings.

item.title: Man shot by ICE in Austin is now in federal custody, officials say
item.description: A Venezuelan man who was shot by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in Austin, Texas, on Sunday during a DoorDash delivery is now in federal custody, officials say. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the latest.

item.title: Iran's early attacks on Bahrain caught Navy families and sailors by surprise
item.description: The scale and duration of Iran's response appeared to take the U.S. goverenment by surprise, three sources who were in Bahrain at the time told CBS News, in part because families hadn't yet been required to evacuate.

item.title: Bill Gates says Trump's AI views point to societal blind spot
item.description: "Most of society is still not aware of how quickly it's moving," Gates said of the latest advances in artificial intelligence.

item.title: JB Pritzker reveals GLP-1 use, pressed on possible presidential run
item.description: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker revealed to "CBS Mornings" that for the last two years he has been using a GLP-1 medication to lose weight.

item.title: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen expand strikes to Saudi Arabia, alarming the U.S.
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen say they launched attacks against Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. CBS News' Holly Williams has more.

item.title: After 9 women murdered, police link 1 death to possible love triangle
item.description: The discovery of the nine bodies has fueled fear and anger, as authorities investigate whether a serial killer or killers were responsible.

item.title: New poll shows Americans are worried about AI harm before midterms
item.description: Recent polling data shows that a large portion of Americans believe AI models could be used by other countries to harm humans. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto breaks down the numbers.

item.title: No Trump TV pool coverage today after he bans 3 major news outlets
item.description: There will be no television pool coverage of President Trump on Monday after he banned three major news outlets from the White House. CBS News' Nanc Cordes explains.

item.title: Key French diplomat explains impact of Trump's Iran war
item.description: Éléonore Caroit, France's delegate minister to the minister for Europe and foreign affairs, joins CBS News with more on French priorities ahead of the United Nations General Assembly and as the war in Iran continues to impact U.S. allies.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue to restore White House access
item.description: The three news organizations, which were banned from White House grounds by President Trump, are arguing that the ban is unconstitutional.

item.title: Converse pulls sneaker ad after critics say it uses racist imagery
item.description: Nike-owned Converse acknowledged that an ad for its Chuck Taylor sneaker is "deeply upsetting."

item.title: Criminologists on whether Patrick Clancy's 60 Minutes interview will change people's opinions
item.description: Meghan Sacks and Amy Shlosberg, criminologists and professors of criminology at Fairleigh Dickinson University, join "CBS Mornings" to break down Patrick Clancy's "60 Minutes" interview.

item.title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man in Austin, Texas
item.description: The lawyer for the man identified him as a 28-year-old Venezuelan national, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez. Officials said he was shot at least once in the torso and was in serious but stable condition.

item.title: Hunter fatally shoots woman he mistook for a deer, police say
item.description: A man shot and killed a woman in Delaware last week, after he mistook her for a deer, police said.

item.title: Patrick Clancy opens up about grief, his children and moving forward
item.description: In the first interview since his ex-wife's murder trial, Patrick Clancy describes what happened at home before his children were killed and how he handled his grief in the aftermath.

item.title: 2026 midterm election races to watch
item.description: CBS News has identified nine key Senate and 42 House races that will likely decide the majority — all of which can change during the midterm campaign.

item.title: Full interview: Hugging Face co-founder and CEO Clem Delangue
item.description: Watch Margaret Brennan's full interview Hugging Face Co-Founder and CEO Clem Delangue, a portion of which aired on July 19, 2026, about the recent hack of their systems by an autonomous AI agent from an OpenAI training model.

item.title: CBS News poll finds more oppose than favor data centers in their area
item.description: Most Americans expect data centers to negatively impact the environment, local resources, although some see economic benefits
